summary: Console usage ledger shows negative-day offset after background compaction rewrite causing alert suppression
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightCart reports that the Console 'Usage Ledger' tile for their org shows a negative offset (yesterday's usage dropping by ~18k token units) immediately after our nightly compaction/partition rewrite. This coincides with a customer-configured alert that suppresses when reported daily usage decreases by more than 10% - causing an important budget-alert to not fire.

Impact: Enterprise customer billing/usage dashboard data appears to shift retroactively, causing trust issues and missed alerts. Affected a single org in us-east-1 but likely affects any org whose hourly ingest was rewritten during the compaction window.

Environment: Hosted production, us-east-1. BrightCart org id: org_0b3f7. Affected console view: Console > Billing > Usage Ledger (daily rollup). Nightly compaction job: ingest-compact-v2 (runs 03:00-03:30 UTC).

Observed behavior: After compaction job completes, the console daily usage graph shows a sudden decrease for the previous day, sometimes going negative when combined with route-level corrections. The affected ledger rows in the raw export have 'delta' values that appear to be applied twice (one from live ingest, one from rewrite).

Expected behavior: Compaction should only backfill missing historical rows and not alter already-committed daily rollup totals displayed in Console. Alerts based on daily usage should only evaluate against final committed values without transient negative deltas.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Monitor an org with high cardinality API-key traffic through the compaction window (us-east nightly).
2) Export "Usage Ledger" CSV before compaction.
3) Let ingest-compact-v2 run.
4) Re-export Usage Ledger for the same date range and compare.

Temporary workaround: Disable auto-alert suppression threshold until fix is deployed or schedule critical alerts to use a 3-day rolling aggregate. For BrightCart we have temporarily disabled the "suppress on negative drop" rule and set a rolling 72h window.
steps_to_reproduce: Export Usage Ledger CSV for org before compaction (Console > Billing > Export)
Allow ingest-compact-v2 to run during maintenance window
Export Usage Ledger CSV after compaction
Compare per-route/per-key deltas and daily rollups - observe negative correction rows and double-applied adjustments

root_cause: A race condition between ingest-compact-v2 rewrite job and the live-aggregator led to duplicate adjustment records being applied to the daily rollup materialized view. Compact rewrite used an upsert path that did not merge with an existing interim adjustment marker, causing a net negative delta when combined with live ingestion corrections.
fix_plan: Short term: run targeted reconciliation job for affected orgs to re-calc daily rollups from raw events (completed for BrightCart and sampled orgs).
Medium term (PR landed): change compact-rewrite to perform merge-on-key and update rollup.version atomically to avoid double-apply (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/2891).
Long term: Add invariant test for compaction vs live-aggregator reconciliation in nightly integration tests; update alert evaluator to read from materialized_daily_rollup only.
resolution: Partial fix deployed 2026-03-11: PR merged to guard upsert/merge logic and a reconciliation job ran for known affected orgs. Alert evaluator change scheduled for 2026-03-17. Customer BrightCart was notified, reconciled, and confirmed their dashboard matches expected totals. Monitoring for similar events increased during next three compaction windows.

Add integration test covering compaction + live-ingest race (owner: ingest team) - target end of Q2 2026
Run reconciliation sweep for orgs with >100k daily token variance during last 7 days (owner: data-ops) - run weekly for 4 weeks
